citations.assessment: Abba rules to Kala. Rashi calls Kala a person’s name, while Tosafot calls it a sage’s name and rejects a reading that would mean leniently.
Rashi explicitly calls the expression a personal name.
This gloss retains the name against the possible competing spelling.
The Yerushalmi names the southerner and identifies his master. The question is put by R. Zeura. Keep the Bavli and Yerushalmi occurrences distinct.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015
